status: User accepted the 1 exact diagnostic sites on 2026-10-07. Focused qualification and its recorded limits are unchanged. Full RPM and native architecture qualification remain separate gates.
root_cause: GCC loses the relation between is_optional and optional_link_begin across the property/call parsing loop. The only assignment of true to is_optional is preceded by initialization of optional_link_begin; the only read of that position is guarded by is_optional.
source_review: is_optional begins false. The question-period branch sets optional_link_begin before setting is_optional=true, including paths that continue to bracket/call parsing.
The source-range recording block executes only if is_optional, then resets it false. Ordinary properties/calls therefore do not read an old or uninitialized position.
Repeated question-period, question-period followed by period, and templates inside an optional chain return a failure before recording a source range.

coverage.matrix: All combinations of 1–4 links drawn from ordinary property/bracket/call/spread-call, optional property/bracket/call and tagged template; both identifier/function-literal roots and varied source offsets. Independently generated expected ranges, optional flags, call/property/spread counts and invalid chain exits.
coverage.compiler: Neither smaller compiler mode reproduces the full-build warning; both compile without diagnostics.
coverage.memory: Both native memory runs have zero errors and all allocations freed.
coverage.actual_node: Lazy/eager parsing checks nullish and falsy roots, missing properties, optional calls, argument/key/getter side effects, receiver binding, Unicode keys, private fields, parenthesized chain boundaries and invalid optional-chain syntax.

limits: The complete loop from optional_chaining initialization through its return is verbatim. Scanner, AST factory and source-range recorder use typed adapters.
The full-build warning is supported by the source invariant and execution controls, not reproduced by the smaller control.
Native property-name adapters accept private names without scope resolution; actual class tests separately check private-field success, nullish access and wrong-receiver rejection.
General scanner recovery, eval scope tracking and full argument/expression parsing are outside the adapter; actual JavaScript checks exercise language-level parsing.
No runtime patch, suppression or compiler-flag change is proposed.
